text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: An institutional records office files paperwork by logging each document in a date-stamped register, assigning a unique identifier, and routing items to designated processing channels for verification, approval, and archiving in strict sequential order.

2) What occurred: On a dated day, the actor submitted a duplicate of the digital ticket file into the transfer channel, leaving the secondary verification field unsigned. The actor then generated additional copies of the same ticket file, leaving the serial number uniqueness check blank. A third document was prepared for the buyer's channel, leaving the primary authentication signature unsigned. A fourth document was routed through the refund exception channel, leaving the authorization code field blank. A fifth document was filed with the chargeback dispute register, leaving the investigator sign-off unsigned. A sixth document was placed in the identification log, leaving the biometric match field blank.

3) Materials/access observed: The workspace contained a single digital ticket file, a set of duplicate file copies, and access to the transfer, refund, dispute, and identification logging channels. No external hardware or network artifacts were noted beyond the file system.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The register showed six separate date-stamped entries referencing the same ticket identifier. Five fields remained unsigned across the distinct documents. The serial number uniqueness check was recorded as blank in the duplicate file. The biometric match field contained no data in the identification log entry.
